title: Ivanti Patches 10 Flaws Across EPMM, Neurons ITSM and Sentry Including Unauthenticated RCE
content_md: Ivanti has released security advisories for ten vulnerabilities across Endpoint Manager Mobile (EPMM) , Neurons for ITSM, and Sentry, including flaws that could enable unauthenticated remote code execution (RCE) and administrative access. The disclosures, published September 8, 2026, span mobile device management, IT service management, and gateway infrastructure used in enterprise environments. The EPMM advisory addresses CVE-2026-18851, a high-severity missing authorization vulnerability with a CVSS score of 8.8. Classified as CWE-862, the flaw allows a remote authenticated attacker to elevate privileges to full administrator-level access. Ivanti Patches 10 Flaws Across EPMM, Neurons ITSM and Sentry Affected EPMM releases include versions 12.9.0.1 and earlier, 12.8.0.3 and earlier, and builds prior to 12.10.0.0. Ivanti has issued fixes in versions 12.10.0.0, 12.9.0.2, and 12.8.0.4. The most serious issues affect Ivanti Neurons for ITSM , where eight vulnerabilities can lead to server-side code execution. CVE-2026-12744 and CVE-2026-12745 are critical deserialization-of-untrusted-data flaws, tracked under CWE-502. Each carries a CVSS score of 9.8 and can be exploited remotely without authentication to execute arbitrary code on a vulnerable Neurons for ITSM server. Three further deserialization flaws, CVE-2026-12648, CVE-2026-12650, and CVE-2026-12651, require an authenticated attacker but may also result in RCE.
